text:
marta: Quick sync request — we need a minimal console panel for continuous-batching health before the Dedicated rollout next sprint. Key signals I care about: batch size distribution, batch wait (p50/p95), fill_rate, queue saturation indicators per-route. Also need clear ownership for runtime vs infra metrics and sample PromQL so dashboards can be wired by Monday.

kevin: Can you clarify what "fill_rate" means in this context? Is that fraction of batch slots filled (avg over window) or something else? And which component should emit which metric — proxy/dispatcher/worker?

raj: From runtime: we can emit these fairly cheaply:
- batch_size (histogram) by (route, pool)
- batch_wait_seconds (histogram) by (route, pool)
- batch_fill_ratio (gauge 0..1) by (route, pool, agg=avg)
- queue_length (gauge) by (route, pool, instance)
- dispatch_saturation (gauge 0..1) by (pool)
We'll emit at dispatcher with route tags; workers already export instance util.

jess: For Console UX we need: p50/p95 wait, avg batch size, share of tiny batches (< min_batch_size), and a discrete saturation signal (boolean-looking) so customers see when routing/pool is stressed. Also add a linkable rollout id so product can correlate regressions with model/route rollouts.

marta: By "fill_rate" I mean avg(batch_slots_filled / batch_slots_available) per batch window. We care about both absolute fill and distribution (e.g., many tiny batches vs few full ones).

kevin: OK. A few sample PromQL snippets to get started (feel free to tweak metric names):
```
# p95 batch wait per route (5m window)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_wait_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

# avg batch size per route (5m)
sum(rate(batch_size_sum[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(batch_size_count[5m])) by (route)

# percent of batches below min_size (needs exporter tag min_size or record client-side)
sum(rate(batch_small_count[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(batch_size_count[5m])) by (route)

# avg fill ratio (0..1) per route
avg_over_time(batch_fill_ratio[5m]) by (route)

# simple saturation indicator: fraction of time fill_ratio > 0.9 in 10m window (approx)
sum_over_time((batch_fill_ratio > 0.9)[10m:]) / (10 * 60)
```
Note: the last one uses Prom semantics — we might prefer a recording rule that emits a `route_saturation_percent` gauge to simplify dashboarding/alerts.

sam: Cardinality warning: route+model_version+pool+instance will explode. For dashboards start with route and pool (and optionally model_family). Avoid version-level tags for 1:1 dashboards. For alerting we can add route_version only when investigating.

console-ux-bot: Suggestion: show two rows in the panel — "Distribution" (histogram heatmap of batch_size) and "Signals" (p95 wait, avg fill ratio, saturation boolean). Each route row should have an inline link to the rollout history for quick triage.

raj: On ingestion: we'll add batch_size_{bucket,sum,count}, batch_wait_seconds_* and batch_fill_ratio to the metrics exporter. We can add a recording rule group: `continuous_batch:route:p95_wait` etc. I'll open a PR to runtime metrics in ~2 days.

kevin: Alerts: propose `batch_saturation_high` when route_saturation_percent > 0.6 for 10m AND p95 wait > 500ms. Keep alert noisy threshold conservative while we iterate.

jess: UX: add a small "what to do" checklist when saturation is high: 1) check pool utilization, 2) increase target pool size or apply fallback route, 3) inspect recent rollout ids. Those should link to docs/runbooks.

infra-bot: alert created: batch_saturation_high for route=chat-completions-prod at 1756789300 - firing

marta: Thanks — looks good. Action items:
- raj: PR to runtime exporter + recording rules (ETA: 2d)
- kevin: recording rule templates & alert definition (ETA: 3d)
- jess/console-ux-bot: dashboard panels + rollout link design (ETA: next Wed)
- sam: cardinality review + final tag set (ETA: 2d)
- marta: coordinate rollout visibility and add to runbook (ETA: next Mon)

Can folks ack with +1 and if any owner thinks timeline is off speak now.

kevin: +1
raj: +1
jess: +1
sam: +1 (will ping if tag set needs to change)

marta: Great — I'll follow up with a meeting invite if needed. We'll start with route+pool tags and iterate. Thanks team :thumbsup:
